label: Carbon monoxide
summary: Carbon monoxide (CO) comes from anything that burns: generators, engines, stoves, barbecues, heaters, charcoal and wood. You can't see, smell or taste it. In a closed space it kills in minutes to hours, often while people sleep, and it builds up in garages, tents, basements and vehicles even with a door open.
signs: Headache, dizziness, nausea, tiredness or confusion
Several people or pets ill at once, and better when they go outside
Yellow, sooty flames instead of blue; soot around a heater or flue
Stuffy air and condensation on windows where something is burning
do: Run generators and engines outdoors, at least 6 m from doors, windows and vents, with the exhaust pointing away
Vent every stove and heater to the outside, and keep a fresh-air opening as well

Fit a battery CO alarm in every sleeping area; take them from abandoned homes, but check the replace-by date (sensors wear out after about 7–10 years) and fit fresh batteries: the test button only checks the beeper, not the sensor
Turn off burners and heaters before sleeping unless they are properly flued
Get everyone outside at once if the alarm sounds or anyone has these symptoms
If you must run a stopped vehicle for heat, clear snow and mud from the exhaust pipe, open a window a little, and run it only about 10 minutes each hour
dont: Don't run a generator, engine or charcoal grill indoors, in a garage, tent or basement, or under a tarp, even with doors open
Don't heat a room with a gas oven or camp stove
Don't sleep in a running vehicle or next to an unflued heater
Don't ignore a headache that gets better outside
ppe: Dust masks and respirators do nothing against CO
firstAid: Get the person into fresh air at once; open doors and windows, but don't become a second victim
Turn off the source if you can do it quickly
If they aren't breathing normally, start CPR
Anyone who passed out, is confused, has chest pain, or is pregnant needs medical care and oxygen
Headaches and memory problems can appear days later
